summary: This section explains the duties of company staff and the powers of officers during a company inspection or inquiry. Company staff must give all requested documents, information, and help to the Registrar or inspector. If staff disobey orders, they face strict punishment including jail and losing their job.
points: Every director, officer, and employee must produce all requested books and papers to the Registrar or inspector.
Staff must give statements, information, and explanations in the required form and help with the inspection.
The Registrar or inspector may copy documents and place marks of identification on them.
The Registrar or inspector has the same powers as a civil court to order document production, summon people, examine them on oath, and inspect books.
Disobeying directions is punishable with up to one year of imprisonment and a fine between twenty-five thousand and one lakh rupees.
A convicted director or officer is deemed to have vacated their office and is disqualified from holding an office in any company.
example: Mr. Sharma, an inspector, visits Meera Textiles Private Limited to conduct an inspection of company accounts. He asks Ms. Gupta, a company director, to produce the ledger books and explain certain entries. According to the law, Ms. Gupta has a clear duty to show all documents, provide the required explanations, and help Mr. Sharma. Mr. Sharma uses his powers to make copies of the books and place marks of identification on them. If Ms. Gupta refuses to obey these directions or fails to attend when summoned, she can face imprisonment up to one year, a fine, and will lose her office as director.

terms.meaning: An officer appointed by the government to keep company records and oversee company matters.
An official appointed to examine company affairs.
